probes.question: True or false: pitch, though it looks solid, is a highly viscous fluid.
The pitch's viscosity is estimated at approximately 230 billion times that of what?

image.alt: The University of Queensland pitch drop experiment: a funnel of black pitch under a glass bell jar with a drop forming above a beaker
image.credit: University_of_Queensland_Pitch_drop_experiment.jpg: John Mainstone derivative work: Amada44 / Wikimedia Commons

panels.text: In 1927, Thomas Parnell of the University of Queensland in Brisbane, Australia, poured a heated sample of pitch into a sealed funnel.
His aim was to show students that some substances which appear solid are highly viscous fluids.
Pitch is a highly viscous liquid that appears solid. Its viscosity has been estimated at approximately 230 billion times that of water.
The first drop fell in December 1938. The ninth drop snapped away from the funnel in April 2014. Slow, but it flows.
